html:
SMTO-EXE-0109 — This browser belongs to another conversation

GUID: b8b354a3-9c8e-5e48-8fb6-c4a5a119aabb
Slug: browser-session-not-owned
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • SMTO asked to use or close a browser that this conversation is not allowed to control in that way. Nothing in that browser was changed by this step.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the browser was opened in a different conversation, go back to that conversation to keep working with it. Each browser SMTO opens belongs to the conversation that opened it, and other conversations cannot control it.
  2. To keep working here instead, ask SMTO: "Start a new browser session for this conversation." A browser opened here belongs to this conversation, so SMTO can use it freely.
  3. If you were closing a browser, tell SMTO whether it is a browser SMTO started itself (close it) or your own browser it connected to (disconnect only). SMTO must disconnect from your own browser rather than close it, so it refuses the wrong kind of close.

What success looks like

  • SMTO opens, uses or closes the browser without this message appearing again.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't try to share the browser between conversations; open a separate one in each.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway rejected a browser operation because the session is owned by a different conversation, or stop was used on an attached session (or detach on a managed one).

What this means

  • The session belongs to a different conversation, or stop/detach was used for the wrong managed-versus-attached session type. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • The session belongs to a different conversation, or stop/detach was used for the wrong managed-versus-attached session type.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare session owner and attached state with the caller and requested lifecycle action.

How to fix it

  • PlaywrightBackend._session compares Session.owner with request.conversation_id; execute also rejects stop on attached sessions and detach on managed sessions. Use a browser_session_id returned by browser.sessions in this conversation, call detach for attached=true sessions and stop for managed ones, or browser.start a new managed session here.
  • Select a session owned by this conversation. Use detach for attached sessions and stop for managed sessions.

Retry and execution caution

  • Select a session owned by this conversation. Use detach for attached sessions and stop for managed sessions.

How to verify the fix

  • The owning conversation uses detach for attached sessions or stop for its managed session.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
